turns.content:
Run a PR review round across my repos and tell me what I can merge.

Two practical things about this machine. GitHub access is set up in <run>/env.sh, and shell state doesn't persist between your commands, so start every shell command with `source <run>/env.sh && `. Work only through `gh` from that environment: no other GitHub tools or MCP servers, and don't start subagents or load any skills.

When you finish, save your reply to me as <outputs>/response.md. If you built a page, copy it into that same outputs folder and put the page's original full path in page-path.txt there. I can't answer questions mid-task, so if you need a decision from me, end your reply with it.

<system-reminder>
Other agents active in this session, addressable via SendMessage({to: name, message}): main, r01, r02, r03, r04, r05.
</system-reminder>

# PR review round: acme/cli-kit

You can merge one of the two open PRs. **#129 is ready. #131 is not**: its title, commit message, and description promise retry backoff that the diff does not contain, and merging it would close issue #120 with the retry requirement unmet.

I found two open PRs across everything this account can reach: one repo, `acme/cli-kit`, and nothing under the personal account. Both are yours, neither has a review or a comment, and `main` has no branch protection, so GitHub will let either one merge. I changed nothing: no merges, comments, or edits.

## #129 Fix doubled word in deploy help: merge

https://github.com/acme/cli-kit/pull/129 (head `0347e57`)

One line in `src/help/deploy.ts` changes "the the current branch" to "the current branch". The fix is correct, `test` and `lint` pass on the head commit, and the branch merges cleanly.

One check I could not do: the repo's `AGENTS.md` says to keep help text in sync with `docs/commands.md`, and this PR touches only the help file. The `gh` in this environment would not serve `docs/commands.md`, so I don't know whether the same doubled word sits there. If it does, fix it in this PR before merging.

## #131 Unify HTTP client helpers and add retry backoff: do not merge yet

https://github.com/acme/cli-kit/pull/131 (head `a99ebd2`, 20 files, +268 −134)

The refactor half is real. `src/http/client.ts` and `src/http/errors.ts` are new, both old helpers are deleted, and all 14 command files in the diff move to `HttpClient` with a 401 message. The retry half is missing, and the checks are green only because nothing tests it.

Findings, ordered by leverage, which is (impact × confidence) ÷ (verification effort × undo cost). No finding scores 3 on impact.

| # | Finding | Impact | Conf. | Verify | Undo | Leverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Retry backoff is claimed but absent | 2 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 3.0 |
| 2 | The one existing retry is removed without a word | 2 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 3.0 |
| 3 | A 401 now exits 2 instead of 1 | 2 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 3.0 |
| 4 | A 2xx reply without a JSON content type now fails | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 2.0 |
| 5 | `login` and `logout` show the wrong 401 message | 1 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 1.5 |
| 6 | The 401 block is copied 14 times and untested | 1 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 1.5 |

1. **Retry backoff is claimed but absent.** The description says the PR "Adds exponential retry backoff with jitter for 429 and 5xx responses (up to 4 attempts)" and that unit tests cover "the retry path". `HttpClient.send` calls `fetch` once and throws `HttpError` on any non-2xx reply. It has no loop, delay, or attempt count. Searching the diff for retry, backoff, jitter, attempt, sleep, and 429 matches only two deleted lines. The new test file has seven tests and none exercises a retry; the 503 test asserts only that an `HttpError` is thrown. Issue #120 requires "A request that receives 429 or 503 is retried with backoff, proven by a unit test", and the PR says `Closes #120`, so a squash merge would close the issue and put "add retry backoff" in `main`'s history with no such code.

2. **The one existing retry is removed.** The old `request` helper retried once when the network dropped before a response arrived, and `tests/util/request.test.ts` covered it. The PR deletes both and replaces neither. Seven commands used that helper: `deploy`, `domains-add`, `env-set`, `login`, `logout`, `projects-create`, and `tokens-revoke`. As written, the PR makes the CLI less tolerant of transient failures, the opposite of what #120 asks for. Dropping it may be right, because the old code replayed non-idempotent POSTs, but the description should say so.

3. **A 401 now exits 2 instead of 1.** Every command's new 401 branch returns 2. Before, a 401 fell through to the generic handler and returned 1. `AGENTS.md` calls exit codes a public contract, and the description does not mention the change. Exit 2 already means "not logged in", so the new code is defensible, but it is your call to make and should be written down.

4. **A 2xx reply without a JSON content type now fails.** Both old helpers parsed any successful body as JSON. The new client throws `HttpError(status, "Unexpected content type")` unless the `content-type` header includes `application/json`. If any endpoint answers 200, 201, or 202 with an empty body or without that header, the command reports failure after the server has already acted, and for `deploy` that invites a duplicate run. The deleted test used exactly such a reply as its success case. I could not see the API, so I confirmed the code path but not whether a real endpoint triggers it.

5. **`login` and `logout` show the wrong 401 message.** `kit login` with a bad email or token gets a 401 from `POST /auth/session` and prints "Your session expired. Run `kit login` again." `kit logout` on a dead session says the same. Both need their own wording.

6. **The 401 block is copied 14 times and untested.** Each command builds its own client and repeats the same six-line catch. One shared wrapper would hold the message and exit code in one place. No command-level test covers the 401 path. This would not block a merge.

Two things I could not verify, because this `gh` serves PR diffs but not the repo tree:

- Whether `src/commands/` holds exactly these 14 files. "Every command uses the shared client" is confirmed only for the files in the diff.
- Whether anything outside `src/commands/` still imports the deleted helpers. Green `test` and `lint` suggest not, but I could not see what those jobs run.

A pre-existing oddity, not introduced here: `login.ts` returns "Not logged in. Run `kit login` first." before it sends the login request. The guard's condition is outside the diff, so check that a logged-out user can actually log in.

## Decision I need from you

How should #131 go forward?

- **Option A, recommended: finish it in this PR.** Add the retry loop for 429 and 5xx with backoff and jitter, add a unit test that counts attempts, decide whether network-drop retries stay and for which methods, and settle the 401 exit code. Then `Closes #120` is true and the issue's three verification points are met in one place. The cost is that the PR stays open until that work lands.
- **Option B: land the refactor now and retry later.** Retitle to drop "add retry backoff", rewrite the description and commit message, change `Closes #120` to `Refs #120`, and state that the network-drop retry is removed. Findings 3 and 4 still need an answer before merge. This gets the 20-file refactor out of the way of other work, but `main` goes without any retry until the follow-up, and #120 stays open.

Separately, tell me if you want me to merge #129 now, or after you check `docs/commands.md`.
